scenes.text: A wonder of the world lies underwater.
scenes.visual: Calm sea from just above the surface; under the pale water, broken columns and giant blocks.

scenes.text: Over two thousand years ago, it rose in Alexandria.
scenes.visual: Map of the eastern Mediterranean and Egypt; Alexandria marked with a star, the Nile delta below it.

scenes.text: Three towers in one, maybe over a hundred metres tall.
scenes.visual: The three-tiered Pharos rising over the harbour island, a small ship below for scale, a hand note '100 m?'.

scenes.text: At night, a fire at the top guided ships home.
scenes.visual: Night harbour; the Pharos with a fire at its top, glow on the water, two small ships sailing towards it.

scenes.text: It stood for well over a thousand years.
scenes.visual: A vertical painted timeline: built (3rd century BC), 956 earthquake, 1303 earthquake, 1477 fortress.
The ground splits open in front of the lighthouse; dust rises, a stormy sky.

scenes.text: By the 1300s, it was a ruin.
scenes.visual: A ruined base of stone on the empty shore in fog; fallen blocks around it.

scenes.text: In 1477, a sultan built a fortress from its stones.
scenes.visual: A square stone fortress with round towers on the same spot by the sea, a red flag on top.

scenes.text: In 1994, divers found its stones and statues on the harbour floor.
scenes.visual: One huge granite block on the sea bed, painted like a specimen plate with notes: 'harbour floor', '1994'.
Dawn over the water; the ghost of the lighthouse faintly painted over the sea, mist washing it back to paper.

scenes.text: It just went under. Subscribe for a true story like this every day.
scenes.visual: Title card: 'Pharos of Alexandria', small painted lighthouse, sub 'still on the harbour floor'.

sources.title: Alexandria, Egypt — French Ministry of Culture, underwater archaeology

youtube.title: Lighthouse of Alexandria: Where Did a Wonder Go?
youtube.description:
The Lighthouse of Alexandria was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, a three-tiered tower that may have stood over 100 metres tall. Built more than 2,000 years ago on the island of Pharos, it guided ships with fire for well over a thousand years. Then earthquakes broke it, a sultan reused its stones in 1477, and in 1994 divers found its giant blocks on the harbour floor.
